hyps.why: Replacing a removed edge with a 3x3 conv adds a whole computation path, a bigger gain than swapping one existing op for another.
Restoring a dead edge into the output with a conv gains more than replacing an existing op.
Giving the direct input-to-output edge a conv instead of nothing is a large gain compared with replacing other ops.
Edge 0 feeds nodes 1, 2 and 3, so reviving it with a conv enables many downstream paths.
Deleting a conv edge loses more accuracy than deleting a pool or skip edge.
Removing a 3x3 conv into the output hurts more than removing a weak op.
Adding a skip from input to output where none existed improves gradient flow and accuracy more than replacing an existing op.
Restoring edge 0 with a conv reconnects intermediate nodes, a large gain compared with swapping ops.
With a skip already on edge 3 providing a residual path, an extra conv on edge 4 adds less.
Adding a conv to an empty edge 0→2 creates a new path, which helps more than replacing an existing op.
